clue.text: Safe outside in plum job

indicators.note: the word for safe sits outside, wrapping around the next piece

parts.note: safe means secure
taken as written

explanation.surface: A cosy, protected position inside a desirable job.
explanation.definitionFit: A sinecure is a position paying well for little or no work, the very model of an easy, sought-after post.

clue.text: Jabs around round's opening for boxers

indicators.note: the word for jabs goes around the next letter

parts.note: shots are jabs, as injections

indicators.note: only the first letter of the word is used

parts.note: first letter R

explanation.surface: Boxers throwing punches as a round opens.
explanation.walkthrough: Boxers are the underpants, not the fighters.
explanation.definitionFit: Boxer shorts are loose underpants, so boxers is a kind of shorts.

clue.text: Fur zealot feeling revolted

parts.note: a nut is an enthusiast or fanatic

indicators.note: turned over, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: an air is a feeling or impression

explanation.surface: An anti-fur zealot disgusted by what he sees.
explanation.definitionFit: Nutria is the fur of the coypu, a South American rodent.

clue.text: Cabinet secretly covering for Tories' leader

indicators.note: in a down answer the first word sits on top of the next letter

parts.note: close as an adverb, as in 'keep it close', means secretly

indicators.note: only the first letter of the word is used

parts.note: first letter T

explanation.surface: Cabinet ministers quietly covering up for the Conservative leader.
explanation.walkthrough: Tories are Britain's Conservative party. 'Cabinet' suggests government, but it is a cupboard or private room.
explanation.definitionFit: A closet is a cupboard or small private room, as a cabinet once was.

clue.text: Imprisoned, others exercised sharing time

indicators.note: the two words share one letter where they meet, so one copy is dropped

parts.note: the rest means the others
trained means exercised, drilled

explanation.surface: Prisoners and others exercising in the yard during the same time slot.
explanation.walkthrough: REST and TRAINED overlap on one T, which 'sharing time' tells you to count once.
explanation.definitionFit: Restrained means held back or confined, as someone imprisoned is.

clue.text: Excited first woman carrying fine daughter

indicators.note: Eve carries, that is holds within her, the word for fine

parts.note: Eve, the first woman in Genesis
OK means fine, all right
D is the genealogical abbreviation for daughter

explanation.surface: Eve, the first woman, is thrilled at carrying a healthy baby girl.
explanation.definitionFit: Evoked means called up or stirred, as feelings are excited or aroused by a memory.

clue.text: Drink vicar perhaps upset over gas?

indicators.note: in a down answer the first part sits over the second
in a down answer, turned upside down, so read backwards

parts.note: Rev, Reverend, the title of a vicar for example
to gas is to talk idly; to mouth is to speak, and 'mouth' is idle talk

explanation.surface: A vicar upset at a drink with fizz in it.
explanation.definitionFit: Vermouth is a fortified wine flavoured with herbs, drunk as an aperitif or in cocktails.

clue.text: Fracking stones securing capital

indicators.note: the phrase secures, that is holds within it, the answer

explanation.surface: Fracking in stone formations to secure money.
explanation.definitionFit: Kingston is the capital city of Jamaica.

clue.text: Serious trouble from wind is astern

indicators.note: the answer is taken out of the phrase, straddling its words

explanation.surface: Sailors face disaster when the wind blows from astern.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wind' looks like an anagram signal for 'is astern', but the answer runs on from its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A disaster is a calamity, a serious misfortune.

clue.text: You, previously found in flower shed

indicators.note: the old word for you is found inside the river's name

parts.note: a flower is something that flows, a river; the Ouse is an English river
thou is the old, archaic word for you

explanation.surface: An old-fashioned person discovered among the blooms in a garden shed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flower' is read as flow-er, a river, here the Ouse in Yorkshire.
explanation.definitionFit: An outhouse is a small outbuilding such as a shed attached to or near a house.

clue.text: Stretches out to see / birds

definitions.meaning: first meaning: ... the neck for a better view

explanation.definitionFit: To crane is to stretch the neck to look, and cranes are tall long-necked wading birds; the verb comes from the bird.

clue.text: You, the French, sample soap?

definitions.note: soap is one example of a toiletry, hence the question mark

parts.note: toi is French for you, with 'French' applying to both words
le is the French for the
to sample is to try

explanation.surface: Invitation to a French person to test some soap.
explanation.definitionFit: A toiletry is an article used in washing or grooming, and soap is an obvious instance.

clue.text: Trunks roughly held by trees' bark?

indicators.note: the phrase for roughly is held between the other letters
bark is the outer layer of a tree, so take the outside letters of the word

parts.note: outer letters give T and S
'or so' means roughly, approximately

explanation.surface: Tree trunks, held loosely by the bark around them.
explanation.walkthrough: Bark is the outer covering of a tree, so 'trees' bark' gives the outer letters of trees.
explanation.definitionFit: A torso is the trunk of the human body, the part without head or limbs.

clue.text: Elope with current partner being reasonable

parts.note: to leg it is to run away, as eloping lovers do
I is the symbol for electric current
a mate is a partner

explanation.surface: Running off with your present partner is perfectly fine.
explanation.definitionFit: Legitimate can mean justifiable or logical, as a reasonable argument is.

clue.text: Quality of stock about right for soup?

parts.note: a mine is a stock or rich supply, so 'of stock' is mine's

indicators.note: the word for quality goes about the abbreviation for right

parts.note: tone is a quality, as of a sound or colour

explanation.surface: Whether the stock is good enough to make a soup.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Quality of stock' reads as the stock's quality, so the possessive puts the word for stock first; 'stock' is a supply, not broth.
explanation.definitionFit: Minestrone is a thick Italian vegetable soup, often with pasta.

clue.text: Organ vessel with detailed wrinkle

indicators.note: joins the two pieces in order

parts.note: a pan is a cooking vessel

indicators.note: de-tailed: the word loses its last letter

parts.note: a crease is a wrinkle

explanation.surface: A church organ and a vessel fussed over in fine detail.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'detailed' as de-tailed, tail cut off.
explanation.definitionFit: The pancreas is a gland organ behind the stomach producing insulin and digestive enzymes.

clue.text: Caught over middle, say, for match

parts.note: C is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for caught
O is the cricket abbreviation for an over

indicators.note: the word for middle is spoken aloud

parts.note: the inside of something is its middle

explanation.surface: A cricket dismissal at the end of an over, mid-match.
explanation.definitionFit: To coincide is to correspond or agree, which is to match.

clue.text: Look, yours truly accepts single's solitary

indicators.note: the two short words take in the next piece between them

parts.note: lo means look, behold
one's, the 's read as part of the word
the setter refers to themself as me

explanation.surface: A single person admitting they are lonely.
explanation.definitionFit: Lonesome means isolated and alone, much as solitary does.

clue.text: Sorry absconder firstly imaginative hiding record

indicators.note: only the opening letter of the word before is used

parts.note: first letter A

indicators.note: the word for imaginative hides the record inside it

parts.note: poetic means imaginative, creative
a log is a record, as in a ship's log

explanation.surface: A runaway who is sorry for concealing a creative account.
explanation.definitionFit: Apologetic describes someone expressing regret, which is what being sorry means.

clue.text: Craft exercise old boy's taken up

parts.note: PE is physical education, exercise

indicators.note: in a down answer, read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: a lad is a boy; the 's is 'has'

explanation.surface: An old boy has taken up crafts as exercise.
explanation.definitionFit: A pedalo is a small pleasure boat driven by pedals, a craft in the sense of vessel.

clue.text: Stone sailor found under boat, oddly

indicators.note: in a down answer the sailor sits beneath the other piece
take the odd-numbered letters of the word

parts.note: odd letters B and A
an old salt is a sailor

explanation.surface: A sailor discovers a strange stone beneath a boat.
explanation.definitionFit: Basalt is a dark volcanic rock, a type of stone.

clue.text: It precedes Mass for verger

indicators.note: the first piece comes before the next

parts.note: 'it' is a coy word for sex, as in sex appeal
a ton is a large mass or weight

explanation.surface: A church official saying something comes before Mass.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mass' suggests a church service but means weight.
explanation.definitionFit: A sexton is a church officer looking after the building and graveyard, a role close to a verger's.

clue.text: Pine, maybe losing heart getting award

definitions.note: used as a verb: to give or bestow

indicators.note: the central letter of the tree's name is dropped

parts.note: a pine is an example of a conifer, hence 'maybe'

explanation.surface: Someone pining and dispirited on receiving a prize.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pine' looks like a verb meaning yearn, but it is the tree.
explanation.definitionFit: To confer an honour is to award or bestow it.

clue.text: Intellectual scoffed following American measure

indicators.note: the word for scoffed comes after the measure

parts.note: liter is the American spelling of litre
scoffed means ate greedily

explanation.surface: A clever person who gobbled after an American measured portion.
explanation.definitionFit: Literate can mean learned or well-read, and so cultured and intellectual.

clue.text: Inventor with zero arrogance taken aback

indicators.note: read backwards, taken in the reverse direction

parts.note: no means zero, none
side is British slang for airs or arrogance, as in 'no side about him'

explanation.surface: An inventor with no conceit at all, surprised.
explanation.walkthrough: 'With zero arrogance' is NO SIDE (having no airs); side is British for pretension.
explanation.definitionFit: Thomas Edison was the prolific American inventor of the phonograph and practical light bulb.

clue.text: Falls about and cheers Queen show

parts.note: ca is circa, about
ta is British for thanks or cheers
R for Regina, queen
an act is a show or performance

explanation.surface: A queen's show at some waterfalls, with cheering.
explanation.definitionFit: A cataract is a large, steep waterfall, so falls is a fair synonym.

clue.text: Prospects of, reportedly, spotted owls finally

indicators.note: the past participle meaning spotted is said aloud

parts.note: seen means spotted

indicators.note: only the closing letter of the word is used

parts.note: last letter S

explanation.surface: Prospects of seeing owls, as reported, at the end of the day.
explanation.definitionFit: Scenes are views or vistas, as prospects are in the sense of outlooks over a landscape.

clue.text: Live, too much inside information propagated

parts.note: to be is to live, exist

indicators.note: the abbreviation for too much sits inside the word for information

parts.note: gen is British slang for information
OTT is over the top, too much

explanation.surface: Excessive inside information spreading through a live broadcast.
explanation.definitionFit: Begotten means fathered or produced, as offspring are bred and propagated.
